title: A Son's Confession
subtitle: Accept changing times, as farmers accept the coming of winter.

trails.title: Special Times
trails.description: Mothers have a gift for turning imagination and a little miracle into a fine meal.

content.text:
Rye Bread
Aged flour, wheat husks, potato skins, a little salt.
Dry and grind the potato skins, then mix them with the wheat husks into the aged flour. Add warm water and knead it into a dough, then bake beside the stove ashes.
The Golden Famine leaves us short on oil and grain, so there's no oil for the bread. The baked loaf comes out hard and bitter, but at least it fills the stomach. Ivan loves smearing chilli paste on top—he says he's eaten it this way since childhood! I've made a note to prepare extra for him next time.

Smoked Fish
River carp, elm twigs, one old newspaper.
Clean the fish, salt it, then smoke it with elm twigs and newspaper until the skin turns black and dry.
The smell carries three houses down, but don't be greedy. Save the fish oil—freeze it for soup.

Grass Roots Soup
Ingredients: Wild grass roots, nettles, half a potato, a pinch of chili.
Instructions: Boil the roots until soft, add chili, stove ash, and salted grass seeds to mimic borscht. The recipe came from a young man I met by the riverside wheat field. He claimed to be a nameless wandering poet.
*Missing Ingredients: Sour cream, carrots, and onions. Can't make proper borscht. Grass roots have been dug out nearly everywhere. I can only forage along the ditches now.

Jam from Neighbor Valia
Note: They hid two jars of real apple jam before the famine hit, and gave me one ... I've tucked it on the top shelf of the cupboard, wrapped in old cloth so the rats won't smell it.
Her husband lost an entire wheat field's harvest ... May the Mother Earth bless this kind couple.

*I've told Ivan to stop bringing food home. The people at the front have it harder than we do.
Besides, in the face of disaster, soldiers and civilians must be treated equally! Even with his position, I won't allow our family any special treatment.

items.text: A Son's Confession

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Faster!
Lilya speeds low across the plain, the newest flying broomstick model cutting a narrow V shape through the grass.

items.speaker: Alpha Two
items.text: Lieutenant! We're losing sight of you!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Then you better learn how to get your speed up to 240 in five seconds.
A series of vague replies come through the communicator, their voices strained as they struggle to catch up to their captain.

items.speaker: Alpha Two
items.text: But at this height, according to the manual—

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The manual? Pft, that's for nerds! Are you nerds?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Move into split formation and prepare to climb! Brooms up!

items.speaker: Alpha Two
items.text: C-Copy that!
Twenty-four Flying Witches follow their leader into the clouds above, slicing the sky in two with their vertical trails.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hold altitude. See the targets by the river?

items.speaker: Alpha Two
items.text: Yes, Lieutenant.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Good. Real enemies won't just stand around and wait for you to strike, but training like this can sharpen your eye.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Flank the target from both sides, avoid friendly fire, and dive!
*boom*
After a successful firing dive, the two flight teams effortlessly reunite in the sky. They rendezvous, hover, and merge into a single formation.
The howl of engines quickly drowns out the commander's conversation as the flight unit descends onto the open ground outside Tamarovka.
With her feet firm on the ground, Lilya passes her broom to her second-in-command.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Captain. Oh, Commander.
The swirling air around her sends Lilya's pristine uniform fluttering like a flag in the wind.
She walks straight toward the cavalry and Foundation leaders, who stand at the entrance of the village, observing the training.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: New broom's nice. Rookies aren't too bad either. Only problem is, they rely on the tech too much. Should spend a little more time on their arcane skills.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Have to say, I never thought I'd wear a Foundation uniform. Wait. Don't tell me I have to follow the Committee's orders from now on.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't worry. You're still on Team Timekeeper. Your new uniform's just for easy identification while you're acting as flight captain.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You have some time to sharpen your little birds, but conflict rides fast. Work quick.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The Foundation swore us enough fuel and ammunition for your entire unit and more besides.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You alone have access to it. No applications, no paperwork, just go directly to the quartermaster.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Nice. I'll make sure the rookies never step foot on the ground.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Irinei said that this is the Su-02ве's combat debut. He hopes to hear some feedback from you.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Well, it's faster, got stronger firepower and better maneuverability. Basically an all-round improvement.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Haven't used it for long, though. Any major defects you know of?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The price.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: One 02 costs nearly triple the amount of an 01, or even more.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Who's paying for repairs?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Me. The Su-02ве assigned to you is the property of Team Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Okay. I'll do my best not to break it.
Noon descends. The sun hangs tilted in the sky, casting an unseasonable dryness across the grassland.
The aroma of simple meals drifts from the households. Whether in times of famine or prosperity, the plain scent of wheat is equally tempting.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: That is all. Dismissed.
With the order given, the high-ranking officials outside the village drift away. Lilya turns to glance at the unit still holding position.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Captain, I need to go take care of the baby birds.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Alright. See you later, Lilya.
The temporary captain of the flight unit turns away.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Anything I can help you with, Commander?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Hungry? Come to my home for a meal, won't you? I'll send for your assistant too.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: My mother's stew could raise a fallen horse. She would love for you to try it.
A simple invitation. Yet under the circumstances, its recipient perceives a subtle unease.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry, I was just thinking about something. Do you mean to say that your home is in Tamarovka?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: That's right. Will you come?
Indoors
The commander pushes open an old wooden door, followed by two special guests.
Faint candlelight reveals a rope strung above their heads where dried vegetables and smoked meat should be hung, but now hangs bare.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Mama.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Vanyusha? Did you bring guests?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good afternoon, madam. I'm Vertin, Timekeeper of the Foundation. And this is Sonetto, my assistant.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Oh! So you're the one—
The elderly lady fails to hide her surprise.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: When Vanyusha told me there would be important guests joining us, I hardly expected them to be so young.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Oh, I mean nothing by it, dear. Just the words of an old woman. Honestly, Vanyusha, you must tell me if you plan to bring growing young ladies to lunch.
Ms. Galina gives a sheepish look at the cabbage soup, hard bread, and smoked fish before her.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We're just here for a simple meal, Mama. No feasts while others starve.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The meal looks delicious, madam. More than enough for us.
Ivan pulls out his mother's chair and helps her to her seat.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Timekeeper, Ms. Sonetto, sit, eat.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: You will have to forgive me. This is all I have to offer at the moment.
Ivan takes a piece of rock-hard bread and softens it in the hot soup. His young guests follow suit.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You have food enough for the winter, Mama?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Oh, don't worry about me. Though, if things go on like this, who can say?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Ms. Timekeeper, are you here to end the famine?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, call me Vertin, madam.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As for this Golden Famine, I will try my best to give it a thorough investigation.
Caught between frustration and hope, the old lady lets out a sigh.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: You should know, Vanyusha, many have told me to leave with them. But I have stayed, trusting that you will find a way.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Some of those fleeing south passed through the village. They said the attackers are different. They only take kalduny—arcanists—as captives.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Arcanists?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Yes. The poor things who refused to cooperate were beaten half to death before they took them. As for the humans, well ...
She simply shakes her head.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But Igor's army would've taken humans too.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Igor?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, you must try this pickled watermelon.
A spoonful of sour, dark-red flesh is suddenly shoved into the chief assistant's mouth, stopping her from revealing any more.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hm? O-Okay.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It really is delicious, madam. Quite different from any I've ever tasted. Might I ask how you made it?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Ah, it warms an old woman's heart to hear such things. Nothing special, really. Though many underestimate the importance of the barrel.
As Ms. Galina steadily shares her years-tested method of pickling watermelon, they leave behind talk of these troubled times.
The sounds of wooden spoons scraping against steel bowls mingle with chewing and swallowing.
The lunch finally ends in an uneasy silence. Leaning against the door, Ms. Galina says goodbye to her guests.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Apologies again for the poor meal.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Hush now. The meal was hearty, and our bellies are full. There are few stews better than yours.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, it was just what we needed, madam.
After her son's reassuring words, the old lady finally closes the door.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I know you have questions, but this is not the place to talk.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Come. Walk with me.
Outskirts, Tamarovka
Outside, layers of golden grass lap at the edge of the village like waves on a beach.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How could Ms. Galina be your mother?
The directness of this question adds a touch of chill to the unusually warm air. The commander smooths a wrinkle in his collar.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Timekeeper, you know the same pain, yes? To witness the "Storm" take away those you love. We all do.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: If that face appeared again, full of light and life before your eyes, could you still your heart?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: When I saw her again, she was no longer my mother, but a teacher with no children, devoted wholly to her students. She never once left home.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The reason for this phenomenon still remains unknown.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: However, observations have shown that each of them has a complete memory, identity, and social relations. Their independent will is undeniable. We can't force them to be the person we think they are.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I know, I know. To speak of the "Storm" would only break her. She would shun me. But in time, she took me as her "child."

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: In the end, I have a mother again. That is enough for me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm glad you figured it out.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Figured it out? Heh, the truth is the opposite, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I chased Galina like a lost pup, hoping to find my mother in her.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: And I did.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Her face, her body, every line and wrinkle—she is the mother I lost to the first "Storm," down to the gentle smile when she talks to me.
The commander takes several deep breaths to stop his teeth from chattering.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Think of it. Those you lost, standing before you again, only their clothes and memory changed.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Would you call them dead and gone? Would you not hold them close, praying memory returns?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's hard to say.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I've never personally dealt with such a thing. Perhaps I'll have an answer if I do.
The commander stops his questioning and turns to the meadow bowing before him, withering amid abundance, stretching endlessly into the horizon.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: It was on land like this that my father first set me on a chestnut mare and showed me the reins.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: My mother watched on—afraid I would fall, no doubt. But she knew this was the way for every child.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: For centuries, the Cossacks have lived by the steppe. She feeds us, she fights us. Rebellion runs free in our blood.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The steppe never changes, nor do her people. Sometimes, I find myself asking: Is this truly a false 1920?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You, Timekeeper, you have lived through many eras. We will never wholly understand one another.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: From what I do understand, you are a survivor of the first "Storm." You've lived through all these eras too. I don't see the difference.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: True. Yet I am marked by my hometown—my own time long before the "Storm" ever struck.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I was forged a Cossack, and a Cossack I remain, no matter the era.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: And you, Timekeeper? Which era is your home? Even 1999 must feel like another world to you.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I do not belittle your path. I only say, losing time and home leaves a wound in the heart.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Politics aside, I respect you. You are the Timekeeper, the master of all ages and all people. Many consider you a savior.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: And I? I am but a man with mortal ties. Zeno has every reason to keep me at arm's length.
This is all the old Cossack has to say. He adjusts his wind-blown hat and makes to leave.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Commander, wait.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Yes? What more is there to say?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have no power to change your decision, but I have a mission here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I need to know. Will you follow Zeno's orders and lead your army to Bereggrad?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I will see you safe to the city and stand with you in your mission. This I swear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I understand.
Commander!
They turn back to see a figure rushing toward them, arms flailing.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Commander, what are you doing out here? I thought you were at home.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: What's the matter?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Th-They got too drunk. A brawl's broken out!
